entries.title: The Sanctuary Charter
entries.body: This keep will be raised as a promise, not a claim. The land will be repaired rather than consumed. No Siegeling will be compelled to serve. Shelter will be offered to those hunted by Raidlord Akhar, so long as they honor the same covenant.

entries.title: Ashes at Riverbend
entries.summary: A forester records the first living flame seen after a grove was cleared.
entries.body: We felled the old grove in nine days. On the tenth, sparks walked between the stumps like frightened animals. The soldiers called them monsters. I remember only that they circled the oldest root and would not leave it. If they hated us, perhaps we had taught them how.

entries.title: The Petrified Root
entries.summary: A fire-blackened root containing a pulse of living elemental warmth.
entries.body: The root is stone on its surface, yet grows warm whenever a Fire or Earth Siegeling approaches. Archivist Pell believes it survived the clearing described by Forester Maren. The Siegelings respond with grief, caution, and something that feels like recognition.

entries.title: The Living Elements
entries.summary: Siegelings arose where elemental power gathered in wounded or threatened places.
entries.body: As human settlements cut forests, redirected rivers, hollowed mountains, and captured fire, the elements resisted. Concentrated elemental energy took living form. Some Siegelings guarded threatened lands; others emerged confused or violent, carrying the pain of the place that created them.

entries.title: Last Watch at the Eastern Wall
entries.summary: A soldier questions whether the creatures outside the wall are attacking or warning the settlement.
entries.body: They strike the quarry road but never the homes. They break the dam gates but leave the fishing boats untouched. Command says beasts know no purpose. I have watched them for six nights, and I fear their purpose is clearer than ours.

entries.title: A Woodlot That Answers Back
entries.summary: The restored Woodlot produces more by taking less.
entries.body: We stopped measuring the grove by what could be cut today. The resident Siegelings showed us which branches would regrow and where the soil still remembered water. Our yield rose. More importantly, nothing fled when our axes came out. That may be the first honest wall we have built.

entries.title: The Quartermaster's Empty Shelves
entries.summary: Storage is framed as restraint: gather only what the Keep can preserve and return.
entries.body: An empty shelf is not failure. It is room held in trust. Maestro's Covenant asked us to become stewards, not owners without limit. Mark every crate that enters, every ration that leaves, and every offering returned to the land. A Keep that cannot account for what it takes is only a raider camp with better walls.

entries.title: The Garden That Asked Permission
entries.summary: Early Valorous learned that cultivation could become a conversation with living elements.
entries.body: The Garden answered not in words, but in warmth beneath the soil, the taste of rain, and a memory of roots left unbroken. Through an Eleminion, the keepers understood the condition: harvest what is offered, shelter what is young, and leave enough for the ground to remember itself. The first essence formed only after they agreed.

entries.title: Embers Under the First Covenant
entries.source: Smith Aven Rook to an unnamed Fire Siegeling
entries.summary: A smith records the difference between commanding elemental fire and working beside it.
entries.body: The old forge chained flame inside stone and called obedience a craft. You taught me to ask. When you refuse, the bellows wait. When you consent, metal bends without screaming and the waste cools clean. Let this hammer remember that the Covenant Card was never meant to be a cage.

entries.title: The Frost-Keeper's Inventory
entries.summary: A humble inventory shows Ice and Undead Siegelings preserving medicine for refugees.
entries.body: Seven bundles feverleaf. Twelve riverfish. Three vials restorative remnant. One place kept open for travelers from the eastern road. The frost bears no binding mark. The resident Siegelings come and go through the north window, and the slate records their names beside ours.

entries.title: Maestro's Unfinished Circuit
entries.summary: A many-element circuit suggests power was meant to circulate through willing partners, never be extracted.
entries.body: No current is drawn from a single source. Fire warms water; water turns the wheel; wind carries the charge; earth grounds it; light reveals imbalance; shadow absorbs the excess. Later hands added every known element to the design. In the margin, a sentence attributed to Maestro remains: power shared returns as possibility; power seized returns as a wound.

entries.title: Names Left at the Gate
entries.summary: A scrap lists families sheltered after refusing Raidlord Akhar's road tax.
entries.body: We paid once in coin and twice in fear. The third demand was for our Siegeling companions. The Keep took our names instead of our people. If stewardship means anything, let it mean this: no living partner listed beside a toll.

entries.title: Shared-Crate Seal
entries.summary: A wax seal marked by both human and Siegeling consent for a fair trade.
entries.body: One side bears Sera Vale's mark. The other holds a faint elemental impress—warmth, frost, or leaf, depending who last touched it. Peddlers on the sanctuary road treat the seal as proof that a Keep still counts gifts and losses without turning either into conquest.

entries.title: Shared Mornings
entries.summary: Daily life with Siegelings is written as consent repeated in small hours, not only in battle.
entries.body: Feed what asks. Nest what rests. Play without forcing notches to clash. The Charter is easiest to keep at breakfast, when no House is watching and a Fire Siegeling waits for the kettle to whistle before warming the hearth.

entries.title: The Yard After Work
entries.source: Resident keeper to an absent sibling
entries.summary: A letter describes Siegelings choosing the yard for song, naps, and stubborn games once the tools are put away.
entries.body: They do not punch a clock. When the Woodlot closes its gates, Earth types roll in the mulch, Ice ones steal the shade by the Fridge, and a Wind Siegeling tries to race the laundry line. If stewardship is real, it must survive ordinary evenings—crumbs, lost toys, and all.

conversations.prompt: These stones remember the old keep. If we rebuild exactly what stood here, we will inherit its mistakes. What should the workers hear from you first?

choices.label: We build with the Siegelings, never over them.
choices.response: Then this place may deserve to outlast us. I will put those words above the yard.

choices.label: First, we make it safe for everyone who reaches us.
choices.response: Practical, and not without heart. A promise is strongest when people can shelter behind it.

conversations.prompt: The old histories call these Siegelings attackers. The records name the felled grove, poisoned stream, and quarry only in their margins. Which account belongs at the center of our Chronicle?

choices.label: Keep both accounts together. Let the contradiction remain visible.
choices.response: Good. An archive should preserve discomfort, not polish it away.

choices.label: Begin with the wounds. The attacks make no sense without them.
choices.response: A clear thesis. Some Houses will object—which may be evidence that it is needed.

conversations.npcRole: Keeper of stores and sanctuary tribute
conversations.prompt: The Houses want our surplus measured in weapons. The residents measure it in repaired ground and people fed. What should the Keep's weekly tribute prove?

choices.label: That partnership can make everyone stronger without taking freedom.
choices.response: Then the tribute will carry both our seals and the marks of every willing resident. Let the Houses learn to count more than weapons.

choices.label: That surplus belongs first to those seeking sanctuary.
choices.response: Agreed. A full vault beside an empty refuge would make liars of us all.

conversations.prompt: The Woodlot answers when we stop treating it like a quarry. Should we teach the Houses that yield, or keep the method quiet until our walls are stronger?

choices.label: Publish the method. Stewardship only works if it spreads.
choices.response: Then we write it plainly. If Akhar's foragers learn restraint before they learn our gate, the land wins either way.

choices.label: Guard the lesson until the sanctuary can defend itself.
choices.response: Caution has its place. I will keep Orin's notes close and the grove closer.

conversations.prompt: The root warms for Fire and Earth alike. Is it evidence of grief, of warning, or of a covenant older than our Charter?

choices.label: Grief first. Recognition without apology is just another claim.
choices.response: I will label it as mourning stone. Let visitors feel the weight before they invent a doctrine.

choices.label: An older covenant. We are late to a conversation already underway.
choices.response: Then the Archive will say we arrived mid-sentence. Humbling—and accurate.

conversations.prompt: Akhar's collectors asked for our Siegeling partners as road tax. We refused. We have little left but need timber for litters and a dry place until dawn. Will the Charter hold for strangers?

choices.label: Shelter them and gift 18 timber for litters.
choices.response: They rest under the Hall banners. At dawn Lin presses a sealed scrap of names into your hand—proof the Charter was kept.

outcomes.response: They rest under the Hall banners. At dawn Lin leaves Verdant Fiber gathered along the road—and a scrap of names proving the Charter held.
They rest, but hungry hands take more kindling overnight than promised. You still find Lin's scrap of names at the gate.
One family reveals a cache they meant for bribes and instead offers Frost Crystals for the icehouse—plus the scrap of names.

choices.label: Trade: 12 timber for whatever they can spare.
choices.response: A hard bargain under soft words.

outcomes.response: They leave Ember Ingots scavenged from a burned wagon—warm still, but freely given.
All they can spare is a coil of Verdant Fiber and a tired blessing.
In the dark, a frightened runner pockets extra timber and flees. Lin apologizes with empty hands.

choices.label: Turn them away. The Keep cannot risk Akhar's attention.
choices.response: Lin does not curse you. That somehow feels worse. Dust swallows the caravan, and the gate feels taller than it should.

conversations.kicker: Among the stumps that remember fire
conversations.prompt: My aunt wrote of sparks that would not leave the oldest root. I carry saplings that ask for timber nurse-stakes—and I can teach your Woodlot which branches consent to cutting.

choices.label: Give 22 timber for nurse-stakes and learn the grove's consent.
choices.response: Kell works until dusk.

outcomes.response: By dusk the saplings take. Kell returns with Verdant Fiber the grove offered freely—and a promise that your axes will be answered, not feared.
The soil is still wounded. Only a little fiber comes free, but Kell marks three branches that will regrow if left.
A blight pocket wakes under an old stump. You lose extra timber containing it, though Kell swears the grove will remember the mercy.

choices.label: Offer 8 timber and ask for cuttings instead of a lesson.
choices.response: A smaller covenant.

outcomes.response: Kell ties cuttings in damp cloth. Verdant Fiber comes with them—thin, honest payment.
The cuttings wilt before the gate. Kell refuses further trade today, leaving only an apology.

choices.label: Decline. The Woodlot is not ready for strangers' saplings.
choices.response: Kell nods toward the petrified places and walks on. The stumps seem to watch longer than they should.

conversations.prompt: I buy what Keeps can spare and sell what wounded ground still needs. Timber, fiber, ember, frost, storm—name a trade, and chance will finish the sentence. Fair warning: the road keeps its own jokes.

choices.label: Sell 20 timber for a mystery crate.
choices.response: Broc's crate lid squeaks like a dare.

outcomes.response: Inside: Verdant Fiber packed in river leaves. Broc grins. "The grove pays debts."
Ember Ingots, still smelling of an honest forge. Broc stamps a shared-crate seal for your Archive.
Frost Crystals wrapped in wool. "For medicine, not vanity," Broc says, sealing the deal.
A humming Storm Cell. Broc looks nervous. "Maestro would call that circulating luck."
The crate holds sawdust and a note: "Toll for the joke." Broc is already halfway down the road.

choices.label: Buy timber: offer 3 Verdant Fiber for wagon wood.
choices.response: Broc weighs the fiber like a judge.

outcomes.response: Seasoned planks stack cleanly in your store. "Grown, not stolen," Broc swears.
Half the load is warped. You still net some timber, and a lesson about charming peddlers.
While you inspect the wood, a latch-hand lifts extra fiber from your satchel. Broc claims innocence too loudly.

choices.label: Browse only. Wish Broc safe roads.
choices.response: Broc tips a battered hat. "Keeps that listen before they buy last longer." The wagon bells fade east.

conversations.npcRole: Descendant of the eastern wall captain
conversations.kicker: On the scar where the quarry road was
conversations.prompt: My ancestor watched Siegelings break dams but spare fishing boats. I carry quarry-glass that can become Frost Crystals—if you will trade timber for a night's honest watch on your perimeter.

choices.label: Hire the watch: pay 16 timber.
choices.response: Torches move along the ridge.

outcomes.response: A quiet night. Tora leaves Frost Crystals cut from quarry-glass and a sketch of tracks that turned away from your gate.
Raiders test the dark. You lose some timber reinforcing the gate, but Tora's warning saves the Woodlot stores—and yields a few crystals.
It was only wind and frightened deer. Tora refunds part of the timber in shame and leaves a single crystal as apology.

choices.label: Trade 10 timber directly for quarry-glass crystals.
choices.response: A clean swap. Tora salutes the old wall's ghost and departs before second watch.

choices.label: Refuse. The Keep keeps its own night.
choices.response: Tora leaves a charcoal mark on the gatepost—the old warning for "creatures with purpose." Sleep comes slower.

conversations.npcRole: Runner for Master Builder Orin Slate
conversations.prompt: Orin says your Woodlot learned to ask. He wants a timber sample of consented cuts—and in return I can leave cultivation binders or, if the sample fails his test, take a forfeit for wasting the lesson.

choices.label: Send 15 timber of consented cuts.
choices.response: Nell weighs each plank.

outcomes.response: Orin's seal returns with the courier: cultivation binders and Verdant Fiber treated for graft work.
Half the load was cut too eagerly. Orin keeps a forfeit of timber credit but still sends a smaller fiber packet.
The grain remembers fear. Orin rejects the sample; Nell returns empty-handed and asks you to read the field note again.

choices.label: Ask for advice only—no timber today.
choices.response: Nell recites Orin's rule: measure the grove by what will still stand tomorrow. She leaves without taking a stick.

conversations.prompt: Sera Vale wants an audit: empty shelves as trust, full shelves as temptation. Offer a controlled surplus trade, or risk the "loose crate" inspection every Keep fears.

choices.label: Trade 4 Verdant Fiber for Ember Ingots under seal.
choices.response: Joss stamps both sides of a shared-crate seal. The ledger balances. Temptation, for once, is named and limited.

choices.label: Allow the loose-crate inspection (RNG).
choices.response: Lids open. Dust speaks.

outcomes.response: A miscounted stack of timber surfaces. Sera's rules say return half to the land-fund and keep half. You gain a modest store bump.
Moisture spoiled a fiber bale. The audit costs you materials—and earns a lecture about stewardship versus ownership.
Someone hid Ember Ingots without a mark. Confiscation feeds the sanctuary forge fund—you keep a share for reporting it.

choices.label: Delay the audit. Ask Joss to return next week.
choices.response: Joss marks the ledger "pending." Sera will remember the pause more than the excuse.

conversations.kicker: Where the soil tastes like rain
conversations.prompt: The Garden that asked permission still asks. Harvest only what is offered and it may gift fiber. Take more, and the ground will reclaim a price.

choices.label: Harvest only what the Garden offers.
choices.response: You wait until the leaves incline.

outcomes.response: Warmth rises through the soil. Verdant Fiber sheds into your hands like a handshake.
Only a little is offered today. Brae says that is still a conversation.
The Garden asks for timber mulch first. You lay it down and receive fiber after the roots drink.

choices.label: Take a heavier harvest while the rows are soft.
choices.response: The soil cools under your palms.

outcomes.response: You pull extra fiber—then watch a row wilt. Brae's silence is the invoice.
The ground reclaims more than you took. Fiber tears, and a young bed dies back overnight.

choices.label: Leave the rows untouched. Thank Brae.
choices.response: Brae smiles with eyes like wet leaves. "Leaving enough is also harvest."

conversations.prompt: Aven taught me to ask flame, not chain it. I can work Ember Ingots from your fiber and timber—if the fire consents. If it refuses, we both pay the cooling cost.

choices.label: Forge with consent: spend 10 timber and 3 Verdant Fiber.
choices.response: The bellows wait, then answer.

outcomes.response: Metal bends without screaming. Ember Ingots stack, waste cools clean, and Rusk chalks Aven's rule above your forge door.
The fire consents only in part. You gain fewer ingots, but no one is burned—including the element.
The flame refuses. Quenching costs extra timber and a ruined fiber wrap. Rusk bows to the no.

choices.label: Force the work: spend 2 Ember Ingots to rush a batch.
choices.response: The old way still remembers how to hurt.

outcomes.response: You gain raw ingots quickly. The Fire Siegelings watch from the door and do not enter.
A cage-spark leaps. Ingots crack, and you lose more than you spent. Aven's letter feels heavier in the Archive.

choices.label: Let the bellows wait. Not today.
choices.response: Rusk smiles. "Waiting is also craft." The apron stays clean.

conversations.prompt: The frost-keepers still leave a place open for the eastern road. I can move Frost Crystals—or medicine bought with them—if you will trust the slate that lists Siegelings beside human names.

choices.label: Fund medicine: pay 3 Frost Crystals.
choices.response: Isse's pack clinks softly.

outcomes.response: Feverleaf reaches the road families. Isse returns surplus crystals the icehouse no longer needs—and updates the slate with your Keep's mark.
Heat on the road spoils a vial. You lose the crystals, but Isse still marks your intent on the slate.
An Undead Siegeling guides Isse past a raid camp. Crystals return doubled, cold as gratitude.

choices.label: Buy cold storage: 14 timber for Frost Crystals.
choices.response: Isse loads the timber for refugee bunks and leaves crystals that will not melt in your Fridge.

choices.label: Decline. Keep the icehouse closed today.
choices.response: Isse leaves the north window latch unhooked anyway—"in case someone needs the cold more than pride."

conversations.kicker: Sparks that refuse a single source
conversations.prompt: Maestro wrote that power seized returns as a wound. I can tune your Storm Cells through a willing circuit—or you can force a draw and learn why the schematic forbids it.

choices.label: Share the circuit: spend 2 Storm Cells and 1 Ember Ingot.
choices.response: Elements answer in turn.

outcomes.response: Fire warms water; water turns the wheel; surplus returns as Storm Cells and a calm generator hum.
The circuit balances imperfectly. You recover a little more than you spent—and a margin note in Sael's hand.
Earth grounds a surge the hard way. Cells crack; Sael bows to the wound and helps sweep the shards.

choices.label: Seize a draw from a single source (risky).
choices.response: The schematic seems to flinch.

outcomes.response: A violent surplus of Storm Cells—and a smell like burned covenant. Sael will not meet your eyes.
Power returns as a wound: cells dead, timber scorched from a flash along the Hall beam.

choices.label: Leave the circuit unfinished. Listen longer.
choices.response: Sael nods. "Unfinished is still honest." The pilgrim follows the wind toward another Keep.

conversations.prompt: The Petrified Root got warm when I sang. It showed me a hollow with old offerings—timber tokens and elemental beads. I can lead you there, but the hollow sometimes takes as much as it gives.

choices.label: Follow Reo into the hollow (RNG).
choices.response: Stone remembers fire.

outcomes.response: Offerings wait like they knew your names: timber stacked with Verdant Fiber and a single Ember Ingot.
The hollow asks a tithe first. You leave timber; it returns Frost Crystals cold enough to ache.
Only an echo of Maren's clearing remains. You lose a little timber to collapse, and Reo holds your sleeve until the dust settles.

choices.label: Leave the root in peace. Thank Reo for the song.
choices.response: Reo pats the stone. It cools. Some doors are kinder closed.

conversations.prompt: The Houses measure Keeps by weapons. I am ordered to collect a timber assessment—or accept a materials offset if your sanctuary can prove partnership surplus instead.

choices.label: Pay the assessment: 25 timber.
choices.response: Calden writes "compliant" without looking up. The Houses will sleep easier; your grove will not.

choices.label: Offset with 2 Ember Ingots and 2 Frost Crystals.
choices.response: Partnership, itemized.

outcomes.response: Calden accepts the offset and, grudgingly, notes "shared current" in the margin. A small timber rebate follows policy.
A senior House seal rejects the offset language. Calden takes an extra timber penalty "for creative accounting."

choices.label: Refuse. Sanctuary surplus is not House property.
choices.response: Calden's smile is thin. "Then the next assessor may bring spears." Dust from the road sticks to the ink.

outcomes.response: Calden's smile is thin, but the spears do not come. Your refusal stands—for this season.
By night, House agents "confiscate" unattended timber near the gate. The Charter still holds inside the walls.

conversations.kicker: A smile that never reaches the eyes
conversations.prompt: A friendly collector offers "protection shares" for timber—or a materials tithe. The accent slips once toward Akhar's camps. Trust is a gamble; refusal may cost more than coin.

choices.label: Pay "protection": 30 timber.
choices.response: The mask dips.

outcomes.response: They leave. For now the road is quiet. You feel poorer in more than timber.
They return before moonrise for a "recount," taking more timber and a satchel of fiber.

choices.label: Offer 3 Ember Ingots and watch what they do.
choices.response: Metal changes hands.

outcomes.response: They take the ingots and miss the Archive. Steward Elara later finds a dropped Akhar camp token in the dust.
The smile hardens. Agents rush the woodpile. You lose timber driving them off.
Vey's mask slips—literally. A deserter presses Storm Cells into your hands and begs sanctuary under the Charter.

choices.label: Denounce them and bar the gate.
choices.response: Spears flash; then dust. The Keep holds.

outcomes.response: They melt into the trees. Your gate stands. Workers cheer softer than they feel.
Before they vanish, a hooked pole steals from the outer timber rack. The Charter holds; the pile does not.

conversations.prompt: A Fire Siegeling refuses to warm the hearth until someone shares breakfast. Mira needs timber for the morning stove—or spare fiber for fruit wraps. How does the Keep start its day with its residents?

choices.label: Cook a shared breakfast: spend 10 timber.
choices.response: Bowls pass between human and Siegeling hands.

outcomes.response: The Fire Siegeling finally breathes on the hearth. Mira finds Ember Ingots cooling beside the kettle like thank-you coals.
Breakfast is a success and a mess. A playful Wind Siegeling knocks the woodpile; you lose a little timber sweeping joy off the floor.
Earth Siegelings bring garden leaves for wraps. Verdant Fiber lands in the pantry unasked.

choices.label: Skip the stove: offer 2 Verdant Fiber for fruit wraps.
choices.response: Cold breakfast, warm company.

outcomes.response: The Fire Siegeling sulks, then accepts a pear. Mira slips you a spare Frost Crystal from the cider bucket.
No warmth today. Mira burns extra timber later catching up on chores.

choices.label: Tell everyone to forage for themselves.
choices.response: The kettle goes quiet. A few Siegelings eat in the yard without you. Mira does not look angry—only tired.

conversations.prompt: Two Siegelings shredded their nest practicing notch-tag. Opal can rebuild with timber frames and fiber lining—or let them sleep on stone and learn the hard way.

choices.label: Rebuild: 14 timber and 2 Verdant Fiber.
choices.response: Opal hums while she weaves.

outcomes.response: The nest holds. Grateful residents leave Frost Crystals they had been hoarding as "shiny cool rocks."
The new nest is too fancy. One Siegeling chews a post for fun; you lose a little timber, but they sleep soundly.
Neighbor Siegelings donate spare lining. You get fiber back and a quieter night watch.

choices.label: Patch only: spend 6 timber.
choices.response: A humble mend.

outcomes.response: It holds until next week. Opal shrugs. "Daily life is mostly patches."
It collapses at midnight. Extra timber goes to emergency bedding, and someone laughs anyway.

choices.label: Let them sleep on stone tonight.
choices.response: They manage. In the morning the yard feels a degree cooler toward you.

conversations.kicker: Soft chalk rings in the dust
conversations.prompt: Young Siegelings want a notch-play circle—no real combat, just direction games. Timber markers and a prize stash keep it safe. Refuse, and they invent rules near the woodpile.

choices.label: Host play hour: spend 12 timber on soft markers.
choices.response: Chalk, laughter, careful notches.

outcomes.response: Nobody gets hurt. A proud Metal-leaning Siegeling leaves Ember Ingots it forged from scrap as "trophies for everyone."
The finale knocks over a lumber cart. Worth it, mostly. Fiber from torn prize ribbons still helps the Garden.
An Electric Siegeling invents a humming toy. Somehow you end the hour with a spare Storm Cell and fewer complaints.

choices.label: Supervise without prizes.
choices.response: The games stay small. Tavi still thanks you for standing in the sun.

choices.label: Ban yard games near the stores.
choices.response: They play behind the Archive instead. A loose shutter costs you timber by dusk.

outcomes.response: They play behind the Archive. A loose shutter and a scuffed beam cost timber by dusk.
They play silently in the mulch and leave you a rude little fiber knot as commentary.

conversations.prompt: Bath day. Water Siegelings want the deep pool; Fire ones want steam stones; someone always "borrows" towels made of fiber. Henna can run a proper wash if you fund it.

choices.label: Fund bath day: 8 timber and 2 Verdant Fiber.
choices.response: Steam, squeaks, negotiated temperatures.

outcomes.response: Everyone shines. Ice Siegelings crystallize leftover rinse-water into Frost Crystals for the Fridge.
Half the towels vanish into nests. You are short fiber, rich in gossip.
A Fire Siegeling overdoes the steam stones and apologizes with Ember Ingots pulled from the cooled rocks.

choices.label: Quick rinse only: spend 5 timber.
choices.response: Efficient, if unromantic.

outcomes.response: Clean enough. Henna marks the slate "adequate stewardship."
They immediately roll in the Woodlot. Mira will want extra timber for floor sand tomorrow.

choices.label: Postpone bath day.
choices.response: The Hall smells like adventure. Henna's look could dry laundry by itself.

conversations.prompt: Siesta hour. Siegelings pile up in sun and shade. Jon asks for timber to widen the lean-to—or warns that without it, someone will nap on your lumber stacks.

choices.label: Widen the lean-to: spend 16 timber.
choices.response: Shade grows. So do the nap piles.

outcomes.response: Quietest afternoon in a month. A Light Siegeling leaves Storm Cells it gathered from static in the blankets.
Someone sleep-chews a support beam. Still better than napping on the storehouse roof.
Residents weave spare Verdant Fiber blankets and gift the extras to the Garden.

choices.label: Let them nap on the lumber—carefully.
choices.response: Dicey.

outcomes.response: It is unbearably cute and only slightly expensive. A few boards go missing into nest upgrades.
The stack topples. Nobody is hurt. Your timber count, however, files a complaint.

choices.label: Wake everyone for chores instead.
choices.response: Productive. Unpopular. A Frost Crystal "accidentally" rolls into the compost.

outcomes.response: They work while grumpy. Output is fine; morale files the complaint in ice.
Half of them nap in the Archive stacks anyway. Pell pretends not to see.

conversations.prompt: After tools are down, Siegelings gather to hum, chirp, and argue about harmony. Lea wants timber risers for the little ones—and promises the yard will feel like a Keep, not a camp.

choices.label: Build chorus risers: spend 15 timber.
choices.response: Blue hour finds a stage.

outcomes.response: The chorus holds. Workers cry quietly. Someone leaves Frost Crystals arranged like notes on the steps.
It is beautiful and extremely loud. A startled cart horse costs you timber in fence repairs—and you would still do it again.
An Electric Siegeling finds the overtone. Air prickles; Storm Cells bead on the riser rails.

choices.label: Sing from the ground—no build.
choices.response: The song is smaller and still true. Lea squeezes your shoulder.

choices.label: Enforce quiet hours instead.
choices.response: The yard goes still. It feels like winning a rule and losing a home.

conversations.prompt: Ramo's Siegeling companion slipped the yard during chores. Help search with timber signal poles and snack fiber—or wait and hope. Daily life includes panic, too.

choices.label: Organize a search: 11 timber and 1 Verdant Fiber.
choices.response: Poles, snacks, soft calls.

outcomes.response: Found asleep on the Storehouse roof. Ramo gifts Ember Ingots from a pouch meant for road bribes they no longer need.
Found muddy and proud in the Garden. You spend extra timber cleaning tracks off the Hall floor.
Found hiding from a loud cart. Needs quiet nest time; Opal borrows fiber and returns Frost Crystals from the icehouse "calm kit."

choices.label: Wait by the gate with snacks.
choices.response: Patience is a kind of search.

outcomes.response: The Siegeling trots home at dusk, offended you worried. Ramo laughs until crying.
A longer night. Torches cost timber. They return before true dark, sheepish.

choices.label: Scold Ramo for careless bonding.
choices.response: True or not, it lands wrong. They search alone.

conversations.prompt: Shedding week. The Hall looks like a pillow fight between elements. Sifa can card the fluff into Verdant Fiber—or you can sweep it into the fire and hope nobody notices.

choices.label: Card the shedding into fiber (spend 7 timber on frames).
choices.response: Combs flash. Fluff becomes thread.

outcomes.response: Excellent yield. The Garden accepts the carded Verdant Fiber like rain.
Mixed elements tangle. You still get fiber, plus a stubborn Ember Ingot that formed where Fire fluff hit the forge scrap.
Everyone sneezes. Frames break. A little timber lost, a little dignity lost, some fiber saved.

choices.label: Burn the drifts for quick warmth.
choices.response: Ash and side-eyes.

outcomes.response: The Hall warms. A Fire Siegeling approves. Garden residents do not.
Smoke drives nap-sitters outdoors. You spend timber airing the Hall and apologizing in snacks.

choices.label: Leave the fluff; call it ambience.
choices.response: Soft floors. Soft lungs. Sifa schedules you for a talking-to.

conversations.prompt: A clutch of young Siegelings needs manners practice: wait for consent, don't chew Charter posts, share shade. Letter wants training toys and snack fiber. Chaos is free if you refuse.

choices.label: Fund manners class: 9 timber and 2 Verdant Fiber.
choices.response: Class is in session.

outcomes.response: They graduate with only one chewed boot. Parents leave Frost Crystals for "the patient Keep."
Recess gets creative. Timber toys become modern art. You still gain a little fiber from destroyed chew-ropes recycled by the Garden.
One Electric youngster learns "wait" on the first try and proudly sparks a tiny Storm Cell into your palm.

choices.label: Observe without funding toys.
choices.response: Letter improvises with sticks. It almost works.

outcomes.response: Almost works. One Charter post gets polite tooth marks.
They learn from older residents instead. No cost but time.

choices.label: Cancel—too busy for pups today.
choices.response: The pups educate themselves on your lumber pile.

conversations.prompt: Pio's Siegeling, Gleam, insists on joining the market errand. They can trade timber for mixed materials—or Gleam might "improve" the deal without asking.

choices.label: Send them with 18 timber for mixed goods.
choices.response: Basket and bell head for the road.

outcomes.response: Fair deals all around. Fiber, a crystal, and an ingot come home with muddy footprints.
Gleam bargains by sitting on a merchant's ledger until prices drop. You gain extra fiber and a minor reputation for chaos.
Half the timber became road snacks. Gleam is happy. Your inventory is philosophical.

choices.label: Send Pio alone; Gleam stays to nap.
choices.response: Gleam protests in three octaves, then naps on your foot.

outcomes.response: Boring success. Pio returns with Ember Ingots and no stories.
Gleam chews a fence rail from loneliness. Timber tax; emotional interest due.

choices.label: Skip the market this week.
choices.response: Pio nods. Gleam steals a crust anyway, which feels like compromise.

conversations.prompt: Hard rain. Siegelings bounce off the walls—literally. Ullo proposes indoor games with timber toys, or you can open the Hall and accept the mess tax.

choices.label: Fund indoor games: spend 13 timber.
choices.response: Rain becomes a drumbeat for play.

outcomes.response: No broken windows. Psychic-leaning residents leave Storm Cells they spun from cabin fever.
Someone invents mud finger-paint indoors. Cleaning costs timber; spirits soar.
Games become story circle. Pell copies nothing down on purpose—and still finds fiber bookmarks left in the margins.

choices.label: Open the Hall and endure the zoomies.
choices.response: Freedom has a mop budget.

outcomes.response: You survive. Barely. A Frost Crystal rolls out of a soaked satchel as rent.
A Covenant banner becomes a cape. Repairs cost timber and dignity.

choices.label: Enforce strict indoor quiet.
choices.response: Rain gets louder than the Keep. So do the sulking chirps.

conversations.prompt: A Siegeling hatchday. Neri wants a small party: timber table, fiber streamers, optional forge-spark cake. Refuse, and they celebrate in the Woodlot with unsupervised enthusiasm.

choices.label: Throw the party: 12 timber and 2 Verdant Fiber.
choices.response: Crowns, crumbs, consent.

outcomes.response: Perfect chaos. Guests leave Ember Ingots and Frost Crystals as presents "for the Keep that remembers hatchdays."
The spark cake is literal. Minor scorch on a table; major joy. Extra timber for sand buckets.
The birthday Siegeling re-gifts half the presents to shy newcomers. Fiber and kindness recirculate.

choices.label: Skip decorations; sing only.
choices.response: A small song still counts. Neri understands budgets.

choices.label: No party—work schedule is full.
choices.response: They celebrate in the Woodlot. Unsupervised enthusiasm invoices you in timber.

outcomes.response: Streamers made of leaves. Also a toppled lumber rack. Happy hatchday.
They keep it gentle after all and leave a single Frost Crystal on your desk without comment.

conversations.kicker: A clipboard held in both paws
conversations.prompt: Kipp, a clever Neutral Siegeling, proposes a chore swap: residents will haul garden fiber if you pay timber wages—or they'll "help" the forge if you stake ingots. Daily life is also labor negotiation.

choices.label: Hire garden help: pay 10 timber.
choices.response: Paws in soil, clipboard satisfied.

outcomes.response: Honest work. Verdant Fiber stacked with tiny paw-prints on the labels.
Union-mandated snack break runs long. Smaller fiber haul, bigger hearts.
They overwater and invent mud skating. You lose timber on boardwalk fixes and gain a story.

choices.label: Stake 2 Ember Ingots for forge help.
choices.response: Sparks and safety lectures.

outcomes.response: A clean shift. Ingots returned with interest—and a lecture about asking flame first.
They make scrap art instead of stock. Cute. Costly. One Storm Cell somehow ends up in the sculpture.

choices.label: Refuse wages—chores are "part of sanctuary."
choices.response: Kipp files this under "humans forgetting consent." The clipboard snaps shut.
